newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan port workers to strike over U.S. sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Japan port workers to strike over U.S. sanctions.

text.p: Japanese port workers will stage a 24-hour nationwide strike on March 12 to protest against the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission's (FMC) decision to impose sanctions on Japanese ships calling at U.S. ports, as well as to seek better labour conditions, officials said on Wednesday.

Two major unions, the National Council of Dock Workers' Unions and the Japan Confederation of Port and Transport Workers' Unions, have decided to hold a 24-hour strike from 8 a.m. on March 12, officials said.
The strike would affect operations at all major ports in Japan, including Yokohama and Kobe, an official of the National Council of Dock Workers' Unions said.

He said the aim was to protest against the FMC's decision last week to slap $100,000 surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports. The FMC said the surcharges would go into effect on April 14 and were in retaliation for what it termed "unfavourable restrictive practices" at Japanese ports.
"The FMC's claim is totally unacceptable to us," said an official of the Japan Confederation of Port and Transport Workers' Unions.
The Japanese port workers' unions are also calling for shorter working hours and job security.
